project.name: conversational-crm
project.idea_input:
Idea 5: Enterprise Sales — Conversational CRM / Relationship Memory Assistant (B2B)
Pitch: A CRM that's updated by talking to it instead of filling forms. After a meeting, a sales rep scans a business card or drops a one-line summary ("met Priya and Arjun from Acme, discussed renewal pricing, they want a demo of module X by Friday"), and the agent extracts the contacts, logs the meeting, tags key discussion points and commitments, and files it into a running conversational thread for that customer. Instead of dashboards, reps ask questions — "what did we discuss last time?", "what did I commit to?", "who attended from their side?" — and get an instant answer pulled straight from that relationship's history. The assistant doesn't just wait to be asked: it keeps an eye on open commitments and proactively nudges the rep when one is coming due ("you told Acme you'd send pricing by Friday — that's tomorrow"). And before the next meeting, a single request — "brief me on Acme" — has it synthesize a pre-meeting briefing from the whole thread: history, open commitments, key stakeholders, and where the opportunity stands.
Relevance: Conversational/agentic CRM that updates itself is a major 2025–26 enterprise sales-tech theme — Salesforce Agentforce, HubSpot Breeze, and a wave of "CRM that fills itself in" startups are all chasing this, because sales rep adoption and data quality have always been traditional CRM's biggest failure point. Proactive commitment-tracking and AI-generated meeting-prep briefings are the natural next layer on top of that, and map directly onto how Experion's own client-facing teams already work relationships across multiple stakeholders and touchpoints.
Scope: Seed few customer accounts with a handful of contacts and a short prior interaction history → capture agent takes a business-card photo or a typed one-line meeting summary and extracts contact details, structuring them into a meeting note → extraction agent pulls out key discussion points, commitments/follow-ups, and next steps (with a due date where one was mentioned) and tags them to the right customer thread → memory/Q&A agent answers natural-language questions over that thread ("what did we discuss last time?", "what did I commit to?") → a lightweight commitment-tracking agent surfaces a "due soon / overdue" list of open commitments across accounts → a "brief me on [customer]" agent synthesizes a short pre-meeting summary from the thread (recent history, open items, stakeholders) → a simple shared view so a second team member (e.g. an account manager) can see and add to the same customer thread → a customer profile view showing the running conversational history.
Treat enterprise-grade access control/governance as a stretch (a single shared team view is enough for the demo), and treat voice-note capture as optional — a typed one-liner is an acceptable substitute for "quick capture" if speech-to-text eats into build time. Keep commitment tracking to a simple due-soon list with no real notification/calendar integration, and keep the pre-meeting briefing to a short generated summary rather than a polished report.
